“Old Zhang, you have spent your whole life thinking yourself clever.

你想到哪里去了？』
Where has your imagination taken you?”

『你，』张胖子嗫嚅着说，『你不是想讨个会养儿子的小？』
“Were you not thinking of taking a concubine who could bear you sons?” Zhang asked hesitantly.

『所以说，你是自作聪明。
“That is why I say you are too clever by half.

哪有这回事？
Nothing of the sort!

不过，谈的倒也是喜事；媒人也还是要请你去做。』接着，胡雪岩便将阿祥与阿巧的那一段情，都说给了张胖子听。
But there is a marriage to arrange, and I still want you to be the matchmaker.” He then told Zhang the whole story of A’xiang and the Wei girl’s affection.


『好啊！』张胖子秀高兴地，
“Excellent!” Zhang said delightedly.

『这个媒做来包定不会「春梅浆」！』
“This match certainly will not become a bowl of ‘spring-plum pulp’.”

『春梅浆』是杭州的俗语，
That was a Hangzhou expression.

做媒做成一对怨偶，男女两家都嗔怨媒人，
If a matchmaker brought together an unhappy couple, both families blamed him.

有了纠纷，责成媒人去办交涉，搞得受累无穷，就叫『春梅浆』。
Every dispute was referred back to him for negotiation, burdening him without end; such a predicament was called “spring-plum pulp”.

老张说这话，就表示他对这头姻缘，亦很满意；使得胡雪岩越发感到此事做得惬意称心。
Zhang’s words showed that he approved of the match, which made Hu feel still more satisfied with what he was doing.

一高兴之下，又将条件放宽了。
In his good humour, he made the terms more generous.


『你跟魏老板去说，入赘可以，改姓不可以；
“Tell Mr Wei that A’xiang may marry into his household, but may not change his surname.

既然他女儿是宜男之相，不怕儿子不多，
With her son-bearing looks, there should be no shortage of sons.

将来他自己挑一个顶他们魏家的香烟好了。
Mr Wei can choose one to continue his family line.

至于阿祥，我叫他也做杂货生意；我借一千银洋给他做本钱。』
I shall put A’xiang into the grocery trade too, lending him a thousand silver dollars as capital.”

『既然这样，也就不必谈聘金不聘金了。
“Then there is no need to discuss a separate betrothal payment.

嫁妆、酒席，一切都是男家包办；
The groom’s side can provide everything—the trousseau, the feast and the rest.

拜了堂，两家并作一家。
Once the marriage ceremony is held, the two households will become one.

魏老板不费分文，有个女婿养他们的老，
Mr Wei need spend nothing, and he will have a son-in-law to support them in old age.

有这样便宜的好事，他也该心满意足了。
Such favourable terms should satisfy him completely.

你看我，明天一说就成功；马上挑日子办喜事。』
You will see: I shall settle it tomorrow, and we can choose a day for the wedding at once.”

『那就重重拜托。
“Then I entrust it to you.

我封好谢媒的红包，等你来拿。』
I shall have a red packet ready to thank the matchmaker.”

『谢什么媒！
“Thank me?

你帮我的忙还帮得少了不成？』
Have you not helped me often enough already?”


谈到这里，小徒弟捧来一大盘油炸臭豆腐干；
Just then the apprentice arrived with a great plate of fried stinking bean curd.

胡雪岩不暇多说，
Hu had no time for further talk.

一连吃了三块，有些狼吞虎咽的模样，便又惹得爱说话的张胖子要开口了。
He ate three pieces in succession, almost wolfing them down, which gave the talkative Zhang another opening.

『看你别的菜不吃，发芽豆跟臭豆腐干倒吃得起劲！』
“You leave the other dishes alone, but how you enjoy those sprouted beans and that bean curd!”

胡雪岩点点头，停箸答道∶『我那位老把兄嵇鹤龄，讲过一个故事给我听∶从前有个穷书生，去庙里住；跟一个老和尚做了朋友。
Hu nodded and set down his chopsticks. “My old sworn brother Ji Heling once told me a story. A poor scholar went to live in a temple and became friends with an old monk.

老和尚常常掘些芋头，煨在热灰里；穷书生吃得津津有味。
The monk would dig up taro roots and roast them in hot ashes, and the scholar ate them with delight.

到后来穷书生十年寒窗无人问，一举成名天下知，飞黄腾达，做了大官。
Later, after ten years of study in obscurity, the scholar won fame at a single stroke, rose rapidly and became a great official.

衣锦还乡，想到煨芋头的滋味，特地去拜访老和尚，要尝一尝，
Returning home in glory, he remembered the flavour of those taros and went specially to visit the monk and taste them again.

一尝之下，说不好吃。
This time he said they were no good.

老和尚答他一句∶芋头没有变，
The monk answered, ‘The taros have not changed.

你人变了！
You have.’

我今天要吃发芽豆跟臭豆腐干，也就仿佛是这样一种意思。』
My wish for beans and stinking bean curd today means something rather like that.”

『原来如此！
“So that is it!

你倒还记得，当初我们在纯号「摆一碗」，总是这两样东西下酒。』张胖子接着又问∶『现在你尝过了，是不是从前的滋味？』
You remember how those were always the two things we ate with a bowl of wine at Chunhao.” Zhang asked, “Now you have tasted them, do they taste as they did before?”

『是的。』
“Yes.”

『那倒难得！』
“That is remarkable!”

张胖子有点笑他言不由衷的意味，
His tone suggested he doubted Hu’s sincerity.

『鱼翅海参没有拿你那张嘴吃刁？』
“Shark’s fin and sea cucumber have not spoiled your palate?”

『你弄错了，
“You misunderstand.

我不是说它们好吃！
I did not say they tasted good.

从前不好吃，现在还是不好吃。』
They did not then, and they do not now.”

『这话我就不懂了！
“I do not understand that!

不好吃何必去吃它？』张胖子说。
Why eat what you do not like?

『从前也不晓得吃过多少回，从来没有听你说过，发芽豆、臭豆腐干不好吃。』
We ate them countless times in the old days, and I never heard you say they were no good.”

『不好吃，不必说；
“There is no need to say it.

想法子去弄好吃的来吃。
Find a way to get better things to eat.

空口说白话，一点用都没有；反而害得人家都不肯吃苦了！』
Empty talk achieves nothing; it only makes others unwilling to endure hardship.”

这几句话说得张胖子楞住了，怔怔地看了他好半天，
These words left Zhang staring for a long time before he could speak.

方始开口∶『老胡，我们相交不是三年、五年；到今天我才晓得你的本性。
“Old Hu, we have been friends far longer than three or five years, but only today have I understood your nature.

这就难怪了！
No wonder!

你由学生意爬到今天大老板的地位；我从钱庄大伙计弄到开小杂货店，
You have climbed from apprentice to great proprietor, while I have gone from senior bank clerk to owner of a tiny grocery.

都是有道理的。』
There is a reason for both.”

一向笑嘻嘻的张胖子，忽然大生感触，面有抑郁之色。
The habitually cheerful Zhang was suddenly overcome by feeling, and his face grew gloomy.

胡雪岩从他的牢骚话中，了解他不得意的心情；
Hu understood the disappointment beneath his complaint.

多年的患难贫贱之交，心里自然也很难过。
They had shared poverty and adversity for so many years that he too felt distressed.


他真想安慰他。
He wanted sincerely to comfort his friend.

因而想到跟刘不才与古应春所商量的计划，
He thought of the plan he had discussed with Liu Bucai and Gu Yingchun.

不久联络好了杭州的小张和嘉兴的孙祥太，预备大举贩卖洋广杂货，
Once they had made contact with Little Zhang of Hangzhou and Sun Xiangtai of Jiaxing, they intended to trade on a large scale in imported and southern goods.

不正好让张胖子也凑一股？
Why not give Fatty Zhang a share?

股本当然是自己替他垫；
Naturally Hu would advance the capital.

只要他下手帮忙；无论如何比株守一爿小杂货店来得有出息。
Zhang need only lend a hand; it would certainly offer more promise than clinging to a little grocery.

话已经要说出口了，想想不妥；
He was about to speak when he thought better of it.

张胖子嘴不紧，而这个贩卖洋广杂货的计划，是有作用的，
Zhang could not keep his mouth shut, and the trading scheme served a particular purpose.

不宜让他与闻。
He ought not to know of it.

要帮他的忙，不如另打主意。
Better to find another way of helping him.

想了一下，倒是有个主意，
After a moment, an idea came.

『老张，』他说，『我也晓得你现在委屈。
“Old Zhang, I know that your present position is beneath you.

不过时世不对，
But the times are wrong.

暂时要守一守。
You must hold on for a while.

我的钱庄，你晓得的，杭州的老根一断，就没有源头活水了！
You know my bank: with its old roots in Hangzhou cut off, its living source of funds is gone.

现在也是苦撑在那里的局面。
We too are struggling to keep it going.

希望是一定有的；要摆功夫下去。
There is certainly hope, but work must be put into it.

你肯不肯来帮帮我的忙？』
Would you come and help me?”

『你我的交情，谈不到肯不肯。
“Between us, willingness does not enter into it.

不过，老胡，实在对不起，饭庄饭我吃得寒心了；
But forgive me, Old Hu: I have had my heart chilled by banking.

你想想，我从前那个东家，
Think of my former employer.

我那样子替他卖力，弄到临了，翻脸不认人。
I worked so hard for him, and in the end he turned against me.

如果不是你帮我一个大忙，吃官司都有份。
Without your great help, I might have faced a lawsuit.

从那时候起，我就罚过咒，再不吃钱庄饭！
From that day I swore never to earn my living in a bank again.

自己小本经营，不管怎么样，也是个老板。』
However small my own business, at least I am its proprietor.”

说到这里，张胖子自觉失言；赶紧又作补充∶『至于对你，情形当然不同。
Realising he had spoken awkwardly, he hurried to qualify it. “With you, naturally, it would be different.

不过我罚过咒，不帮人家做饭庄；这个咒是跪在关帝菩萨面前罚的，
But I swore not to work in another man’s bank, and I made that oath kneeling before Lord Guan.

不好当耍。
It is not a thing to treat lightly.

老胡，千言万语并一句∶对不对你！』
A thousand words come to one: I am sorry, Old Hu.”

说完，举杯表示道歉。
He raised his cup in apology.


『这杯酒，我不能吃。
“I cannot drink to that.

我有两句话请问你，
Let me ask you two questions.

你罚咒，是不帮人家做钱庄？』
Your oath was that you would not work in someone else’s bank?”

『是的。』
“Yes.”

『就是说，不给人家做伙计？』
“That is, you would not be another man’s clerk?”

『是的！』张胖子重重地回答。
“Exactly!” Zhang answered emphatically.

『那末，老张，你先要弄清楚，我不是请你做阜康的伙计。』
“Then understand this first, Old Zhang: I am not asking you to become a clerk at Fukang.”

『做啥？』张胖子愕然相问。
“What, then?” Zhang asked in surprise.

『做股东。
“A shareholder.

等于你自己做老板！
In effect, your own proprietor.

这样子，随便你罚多重的咒，都不会应了。』
However solemn your oath, that cannot violate it.”

『做股东！』
“A shareholder!”

张胖子心动了，
He was tempted.

『不过，我没有本钱。』
“But I have no capital.”

『本钱我借你。
“I shall lend it to you.

我划一万银子，算你的股份；
I shall assign ten thousand taels as your share.

你来管事，另外开一份薪水。』
You will manage the business and draw a separate salary.

胡雪岩说，『你那家小杂货店，我也替你想好了出路；盘给阿祥，他自然并到他丈人那里。
I have thought of a solution for your grocery too: transfer it to A’xiang, and he will naturally combine it with his father-in-law’s.

你看，这不是顺理成章 的事？』
Does that not all follow neatly?”



胡雪岩 · 红顶商人
The Red-Topped Merchant
第六章（本章第5部分，共5部分）
逐句中英对照
原著：高阳


这样的条件，这样的交情，照常理说，张胖子应该一诺无辞；
With such terms and such friendship behind them, Fatty Zhang ought, by all ordinary reasoning, to have accepted without hesitation.

但他仍在踌躇，
Yet he still wavered.

因为第一，钱庄这一行，他受过打击，确实有些寒心；
For one thing, the blow he had suffered in banking had truly chilled his heart.

第二，交朋友将心换心，惟其胡雪岩如此厚爱，自己就更得忖量一下，倘或接手以后，没有把握打开局面，整顿内部，
For another, friendship required feeling to be repaid with feeling: precisely because Hu Xueyan treated him so generously, he must consider whether he could open up new business and put the bank in order.

让好朋友失望，倒不如此刻辞谢，还可以保全交情。
If he could not be sure of doing so, it would be better to decline now and preserve their friendship than to disappoint his friend later.

当然，他说不出辞绝的话，而且也舍不得辞绝；
Of course, he could neither bring himself to refuse nor bear to let the opportunity go.

考虑了又考虑，说了句∶『让我先看一看再说。』
After thinking it over and over, he said, “Let me look into it first.”

『看？
“Look into it?

你用不着看了！』胡雪岩说∶『阜康的情形比起从前王雪公在世的时候那样热闹，自然显得差了。
There is no need!” Hu replied. “Fukang is naturally less lively than it was when Governor Wang was alive.

跟上海的同行比一比，老实说一句，比上不足，比下着实有余。
Compared with the other Shanghai banks, I can honestly say that we fall short of the best but stand well above the worst.

阜康决没有亏空，
There is absolutely no deficit.

放款出去的户头，都是靠得住的；几个大存户亦都殷实得很，
Our borrowers are reliable, and the few large depositors are all substantial men.

不至于一下子都来提款。
They will not all descend on us to withdraw their money at once.

毛病是我不能拿全副精神摆在上头；
The trouble is that I cannot give it my whole attention.

原来请的那个大伙，人既老实，身子又不好，所以弄得死气沉沉，没有起色。
The chief clerk I engaged is a straightforward fellow, but his health is poor; the place has become lifeless and never gets ahead.

你去了，当然会不同；
With you there, things would certainly be different.

等我来出两个主意，请你一手去做，
Let me provide an idea or two and you carry them through.

同心协力拿阜康这块招牌再刷得它金光闪亮。』
Working together, we shall polish Fukang’s signboard until it shines like gold again.”

照这样说，大可一干；
Put that way, the venture was worth undertaking.

不过，『我到底是啥身分到阜康呢？』他说，
Still, Zhang asked, “In exactly what capacity am I to join Fukang?

『钱庄的规矩，你是晓得的。』
You know the rules of banking.”

钱庄的规矩，大权都在大伙手里，股东不得过问；
By those rules, authority rested entirely with the chief clerk; shareholders were not to interfere.

胡雪岩原就有打算的，
Hu had already thought this through.

毫不迟疑地答道∶『对我来说，你是股东；
“In relation to me, you are a shareholder,” he answered without hesitation.

对阜康来说，你是大伙。
“In relation to Fukang, you are the chief clerk.

你不是替人家做伙计，是替自己做。』
You will be working for yourself, not serving another man.”

这个解释很圆满，张胖子表示满意，
The explanation was complete, and Zhang was satisfied.

毅然决然地答道∶『那就一言为定。
“Then it is settled,” he said firmly.

主意你来出，事情我来做；
“You supply the ideas; I carry them out.

对外是你出面，在内归我负责。』
You represent us outside; I take charge within.”

『好极！
“Excellent!

我正就是这个意思——。』
That is exactly what I mean—”


『慢来。』
“Wait!”

张胖子突然想到，迫不及待地问∶『原来的那位老兄呢？』
A sudden thought struck Zhang, and he asked urgently, “What about the man already there?”

『这你不必担心。
“You need not worry about him.

他身体不好，而且儿子已经出道；
His health is poor, and his son has made his way in the world.

在美国人的洋行里做「康白度」，老早就劝他回家享福。
He is a comprador with an American trading firm and has long urged his father to retire and enjoy life.

他因为我待他不错，
The old fellow is grateful for my treatment of him.

虽然辞过几次，我不放他，也就不好意思走。
He has offered his resignation several times, but when I refused to let him go he felt ashamed to insist.

现在有你去接手，在他真正求之不得。』
He could wish for nothing better than to have you take over.”

张胖子释然了，
Zhang was relieved.

『我就怕敲了人家饭碗！』
“I was afraid of breaking another man’s rice bowl.”

他又生感慨，
Once more he grew reflective.

『我的东家不好；
“My own employer treated me badly.

不能让他也在背后骂东家不好。』
We must not make him say behind our backs that his employer treated him badly too.”

『你想想我是不是那种人？』胡雪岩问道，
“Do you think I am that sort of man?” Hu asked.

『老张，君子一言，驷马难追；
“Old Zhang, once a gentleman gives his word, four horses cannot overtake it.

从此刻起，我们就算合伙了！
From this moment, we are partners.

倒谈谈生意经；
Now let us talk business.

你看，我们应该怎么个做法？』
How do you think we should proceed?”

这一下，将张胖子问住了。
That stumped Zhang.

他是钱庄学徒出身，按部就班做到大伙，
He had begun as an apprentice and risen step by step to chief clerk.

讲内部管理，要看实际情形而定；谈到外面的发展，也要先了解了解市面。
Before advising on internal management he would have to examine the actual position, and before discussing expansion he would have to study the market.

如要他凭空想个主意出来，可就抓瞎了。
Asked to produce an idea out of thin air, he was helpless.

想了好一会，他说∶『现在的银价上落很大；
At last he said, “The price of silver fluctuates sharply nowadays.

如果消息灵通，兑进兑出一转手之间，利息不小。』
With prompt information, we could make a handsome profit simply buying and selling.”

『这当然。
“Certainly.

归你自己去办，用不着商量。』
You can deal with that yourself; there is no need to consult me.

胡雪岩说∶『我们要商量的是，长线放远鹞，看到三年以后，大局一定，怎么样能够飞黄腾达，一下子窜了起来。』
What we must discuss is how to let out a long line and fly our kite far ahead: three years from now, once affairs have settled down, how can we make a sudden leap into prosperity?”

『这——』张胖子笑道，『我就没有这份本事了。』
“That,” Zhang said with a laugh, “is beyond my abilities.”


谈生意经，胡雪岩一向最起劲；
Business talk always roused Hu’s enthusiasm.

又正当微醺之时，兴致更佳，
Now, pleasantly warmed by wine, he was more eager than ever.

『今天难得有空，
“We seldom have time to ourselves.

我们索性好好儿筹划一番。』
Let us make some proper plans today.

他问∶『老张，山西票号的规矩，你总熟悉的吧？』
Old Zhang, you must know the practices of the Shanxi remittance houses?”

『隔行如隔山；
“Different trades are mountains apart.

钱庄、票号看来是同行，做法不同。』
Banks and remittance houses may look like the same business, but their methods differ.”

张胖子在胡雪岩面前不敢不说老实话，
Before Hu, Zhang dared give nothing but an honest answer.

『而且，票号的势力不过长江以南；
“Besides, their influence does not extend south of the Yangtze.

他们的内幕，实在没有机会见识。』
I have had no opportunity to see their inner workings.”

『我们做钱庄，唯一的劲敌就是山西票号。
“For us bankers, the Shanxi houses are the only formidable rivals.

知己知彼，百战百胜；
Know yourself and your enemy, and you can win a hundred battles.

所以这方面，我平时很肯留心。
That is why I always pay close attention to them.

现在，不妨先说点给你听。』
Let me tell you something about them first.”

照胡雪岩的了解，山西票号原以经营汇兑为主；而以京师为中心。
As Hu understood it, the Shanxi houses had originally dealt chiefly in remittances, with the capital as their centre.

这几年干戈扰攘，道路艰难，公款解京，诸多不便；
In recent years, war and difficult roads had made it inconvenient to transport government funds to Beijing.

因而票号无形中代理了一部分部库与省库的职司，
Almost without a formal arrangement, the houses had taken over some of the duties of the central and provincial treasuries.

公款并不计息，汇水尤为可观，自然大获其利。
They paid no interest on government balances, while their remittance charges were substantial: naturally, the profits were great.

还有各省的巨商显宦，认为天下最安稳的地方，莫如京师；
Moreover, wealthy merchants and high officials in the provinces considered the capital the safest place under heaven.

所以多将现款，汇到京里，实际上就是存款。
They therefore sent much of their ready cash there, which in practice meant depositing it with the houses.

这些存款的目的不是生利，而是保本，所以利息极轻。
Such deposits were intended to preserve capital, not earn income, so the interest paid was very low.


『有了存款要找出路。
“Once you have deposits, you must find an outlet for them.

头寸烂在那里，大元宝不会生小元宝的。』胡雪岩说，
Leave funds to rot, and large ingots will never give birth to little ones,” Hu said.

『山西票号近年来通行放款给做京官的，
“In recent years, the Shanxi houses have commonly lent to officials in the capital.

名为「放京债」；
They call it making ‘capital loans’.

听说一万两的借据，实付七千——』『什么？』张胖子大声打断，
I hear that against a note for ten thousand taels they actually advance seven thousand—” “What?” Zhang interrupted loudly.

『这是什么债，
“What sort of loan is that?

比印子钱还要凶！』
Worse than the usurers who collect their instalments every day!”

『你说比印子钱还要凶，借的人倒是心甘情愿；
“You think it worse, but the borrowers agree willingly enough.

反正羊毛出在羊身上，
The wool comes off the sheep’s back in the end.

老百姓倒霉！』
It is the common people who suffer.”

『怎么呢？』
“How so?”

『你想，
“Think about it.

做官借债，拿什么来还？
When an official borrows, what can he repay with?

自然是老百姓替他还。
Naturally, the people repay for him.

譬如某人放了你们浙江藩司，
Suppose someone is appointed provincial treasurer of your Zhejiang.

京里打点，上任盘费；
He must make payments in the capital and pay for his journey.

到任以后置公馆、买轿马、用底下人，哪一样不用钱？
Once he arrives, he needs a residence, chairs and horses, servants—what does not cost money?

于是乎先借一笔京债；
So he first takes a capital loan.

到了任想法子先挪一笔款子还掉，随后慢慢儿弥补；
After assuming office, he finds some public money to divert and pays it off, then gradually makes up the sum.

不在老百姓头上动脑筋，岂不是就要闹亏空了？』
Unless he devises ways to extract it from the people, he will be left with a deficit in his accounts.”

『这样子做法难道没有风险！
“But is that not risky?

譬如说，到了任不认帐？』
Suppose he refuses to acknowledge the debt once he takes office?”

『不会的。
“He will not.

第一、有保人；保人一定也是京官。
First, there is a guarantor, who must also be an official in the capital.

第二、有借据；
Second, there is a signed note.

如果赖债，到都察院递呈子，
If he repudiates the debt, a petition can be lodged with the Censorate.

御史一参，赖债的人要丢官。
One impeachment from a censor, and the debtor loses his post.

第三、自有人帮票号的忙，不准人赖债。
Third, others will help the houses and prevent defaults.

为啥呢，
Why?

一班穷翰林平时都靠借债度日；
The poor Hanlin scholars live on loans.

就盼望放出去当考官，当学政，收了门生的「贽敬」来还债；
They hope to be sent out as examiners or education commissioners, collect ceremonial gifts from their pupils and repay their debts.

还了再借，日子依旧可以过得下去。
Having repaid, they can borrow again and keep going.

倘若有人赖了债，票号联合起来，说做官的没有信用，从此不借；
If anyone defaults, the houses may act together, declare officials untrustworthy and stop lending.

穷翰林当然大起恐慌，
The poor scholars would panic.

会帮票号讨债。』
They will help recover the money.”

胡雪岩略停一下又说∶『要论风险，只有一样；新官上任，中途出了事，
Hu paused, then went on. “There is only one real risk: something may happen to a newly appointed official on his journey.

或者死掉，或者丢官。
He may die or lose his appointment.

不过也要看情形而定，
Even then, it depends.

保人硬气的，照样会一肩担承。』
A sound guarantor will shoulder the whole obligation.”

『怪不得！』张胖子说∶『这几年祁、太、平三帮票号，在各省大设分号。
“No wonder!” Zhang exclaimed. “These past few years the Qi, Tai and Ping groups of remittance houses have been opening branches all over the provinces.

原来有这样的好处！』
So this is the advantage!”

他跃跃欲试地，『我们何不学人家一学？』
Eager to try it himself, he asked, “Why should we not learn from them?”

『着啊！』
“Exactly!”

胡雪岩干了一杯酒，
Hu drained his cup.

『我正就是这个意思。』
“That is just what I have in mind.”


胡雪岩的意思是，仿照票号的办法，办两项放款。
Hu intended to follow their example with two kinds of loan.

第一是放给做官的。
The first would go to officials.

由于南北道路艰难，时世不同，这几年官员调补升迁，多不按常规；
With travel between north and south so difficult and circumstances so altered, transfers and promotions in recent years had often departed from normal procedure.

所谓『送部引见』的制度，虽未废除，却多变通办理；
The requirement that officials be sent to the appropriate ministry and presented for an imperial audience had not been abolished, but exceptions were commonly made.

尤其是军功上保升的文武官员，尽有当到藩司、皋司，主持一省钱谷、司法的大员，而未曾进过京的。
In particular, among civil and military officials recommended for promotion on the strength of wartime service, there were even provincial treasurers and judicial commissioners—men responsible for the finances or justice of an entire province—who had never been to Beijing.

由京里补缺放出来，自然可以借京债；
A man appointed from the capital could, of course, take a capital loan.

如果在江南升调，譬如江苏知县，调升湖北的知府，没有一笔盘缠与安家银子就『行不得也』！
But an official promoted within the lower Yangtze region—a Jiangsu magistrate made prefect in Hubei, for instance—could not move without money for the journey and for establishing his household.

胡雪岩打算仿照京债的办法，帮帮这些人的忙。
Hu proposed to help such men with loans on the same model.

『这当然是有风险的。
“There is risk, of course.

但要通扯扯算，以有余补不足。
But we must reckon the whole account, using the surplus here to cover the shortfall there.

自从开办厘金以来，不晓得多少人发了财；
Since the likin taxes began, goodness knows how many men have grown rich.

象这种得了税差的，早一天到差，多一天好处，
Someone given a tax post gains an extra day’s profit for every day earlier he arrives.

再高的利息，他也要借；而且不会吃倒帐。
However high the interest, he will borrow, and we shall not suffer a bad debt.

我们的做法是要在这些户头上多赚他些，来弥补倒帐。
Our method is to earn more from these accounts to make up for losses on others.

话不妨先说明白，我们是「劫富济贫」的做法。』
We can say it plainly from the start: we shall ‘take from the rich to help the poor’.”

『劫富济贫！』张胖子念一两遍，点点头说∶『这个道理我懂了。
“Take from the rich to help the poor!” Zhang repeated the phrase once or twice and nodded. “I understand the principle.

第二项呢？『
What is the second kind?”


『第二项放款是放给逃难到上海来的内地乡绅人家。
“The second is for families of the inland gentry who have fled to Shanghai.

这些人家在原籍，多是靠收租过日子的，
At home, most lived on rents.

一早拎只鸟笼泡茶店；下午到澡塘子睡一觉；晚上「摆一碗」，吃得醉醺醺回家。
In the morning they carried a birdcage to the teahouse; in the afternoon they slept at the bathhouse; in the evening they sat down to a drinking party and went home tipsy.

一年三百六十天，起码三百天是这样子。
Of the three hundred and sixty days of the year, at least three hundred passed like that.

这种人，恭维他，说他是做大少爷；
To flatter such men, you call them young gentlemen of leisure.

讲得难听点，就是无业游民。
Less politely, they are idle vagabonds.

如果不是祖宗积德，留下大把家私，一定做「伸手大将军」了。
Had their ancestors not earned merit and left them great estates, they would certainly have become generals of the outstretched hand.

当初逃难来的时候，总有些现款细软在手里，一时还不会「落难」；
When they first fled here, they had some cash and valuables, so they did not immediately fall on hard times.

日久天长，坐吃山空，又是在这个花天酒地的夷场上，
But spend without earning, and even a mountain is exhausted—especially in this foreign settlement, with its feasting and pleasure.

所以这几年下来，很有些赫赫有名的大少爷，快要讨饭了！』
After these few years, a good many once-famous young gentlemen are close to begging.”

这话不是过甚其词，
This was no exaggeration.

张胖子就遭遇到几个；境况最凄惨的，甚至倚妻女卖笑为生。
Zhang had encountered several himself; the most wretched even depended on their wives and daughters to earn a living entertaining men.

因此，胡雪岩的话，在他深具同感；只是放款给这些人，他不以为然，
He therefore sympathised deeply with Hu’s account, but disapproved of lending to such people.

『救急容易教穷难！』
“It is easy to relieve an emergency and hard to rescue poverty.

他说，『非吃倒帐不可！』
We should be certain to lose the money.”

『不会的。』胡雪岩说，
“No,” Hu said.

『这就要放开眼光来看；
“We must look further ahead.

长毛的气数快尽了！
The Longhairs’ allotted days are almost over.

江浙两省一光复，逃难的回家乡，
Once Jiangsu and Zhejiang are recovered, the refugees will go home.

大片田地长毛抢不走；
The rebels cannot carry off their great tracts of farmland.

他们苦一两年，仍旧是大少爷。
After a year or two of hardship, they will be gentlemen of leisure again.

怎么会吃倒帐？』
Why should the loans be lost?”

『啊！』
“Ah!”

张胖子深深吸了口气，
Zhang drew a deep breath.

『这一层我倒还没有想到。
“That had not occurred to me.

照你的说法，我倒有个做法。』
On that basis, I have a method to suggest.”

『你说！』
“Let us hear it.”

『叫他们拿地契来抵押。
“Require their title deeds as security.

没有地契的，写借据，言明如果欠款不还，甘愿以某处某处田地作价抵还。』
If they have no deeds with them, have them sign a note stating that, if they fail to repay, specified land shall be valued and surrendered in settlement.”

『对！
“Quite right!

这样做法，就更加牢靠了。』
That makes it safer still.”


『还有！』
“One thing more!”

张胖子跟胡雪岩一席长谈，启发良多，也变得聪明了；
Their long conversation had taught Zhang a great deal and sharpened his wits.

他说∶『既然是救穷，就要看远一点。
“Since we are relieving poverty, we must look ahead.

那班大少爷出身的，有一万用一万，不顾死活的；
These men brought up as young masters spend ten thousand if they have ten thousand, regardless of the consequences.

所以第一次来抵押，不可以押足，
We should not advance the full amount on a property at the first application.

预备他不得过门的时候来加押。』
Leave something in reserve for an additional advance when they cannot make ends meet.”

这就完全谈得对路了，
Now they were thinking along exactly the same lines.

越谈越多，也越谈越深；
Their discussion grew wider and deeper.

然而仅谈放款，
Yet they spoke only of lending.

又哪里来的款子可放？
Where were the funds to come from?

张胖子心里一直有着这样一个疑问，却不肯问出来；因为在他意料中，心思细密的胡雪岩，一定会自己先提到，无须动问。
The question had been in Zhang’s mind all along, but he had held it back, expecting so meticulous a man as Hu to raise it without prompting.

而胡雪岩却始终不提这一层，这就逼得他不能不问了∶『老胡，这两项放款，期限都是长的；
Hu never did, however, and Zhang was obliged to ask. “Old Hu, both these kinds of loan are long-term.

尤其是放给有田地的人家，要等光复了，才有收回的确期，
Those secured on land, especially, cannot have a definite prospect of repayment until the country is recovered.

只怕不是三两年的事。
That may take more than two or three years.

这笔头寸不在少数，
It will require a great deal of capital.

你打算过没有？』
Have you considered that?”

『当然打算过。
“Of course.

只有放款，没有存款的生意，怎么做法？
How can we do business with loans going out and no deposits coming in?

我倒有个吸收存款的办法；只怕你不赞成。』
I have a way of attracting deposits, but I fear you may not approve.”

『何见以得我不赞成？
“Why should you think so?

做生意嘛，
We are in business.

有存款进来，难道还推出去不要？』
If deposits come our way, surely we shall not turn them down?”

胡雪岩不即回答，
Hu did not answer at once.

笑一笑，喝口酒，神态显得很诡秘；这让张胖子又无法捉摸了。
He smiled and sipped his wine with a mysterious air that once more left Zhang unable to fathom him.

他心里的感觉很复杂，又佩服，又有些戒心；
Zhang’s feelings were mixed: admiration, but also wariness.

觉得胡雪岩花样多得莫测高深，与这样的人相处，实在不能掉以轻心。
Hu’s resources were so unpredictable that one could never safely let down one’s guard with him.


终于开口了；胡雪岩问出来一句令人意料不到的话∶『老张，譬如说∶我是长毛，有笔款子化名存到你这里，
At last Hu spoke, asking a wholly unexpected question. “Old Zhang, suppose I were a Longhair and wanted to deposit money with you under an assumed name.

你敢不敢收？』
Would you dare accept it?”

『这——，』张胖子答∶『这有啥不敢？』
“Well—why should I not?”

『如果有条件的呢？』
“What if there were conditions?”

『什么条件？』
“What conditions?”

『他不要利息，也不是活期；
“He asks no interest, and it is not a demand deposit.

三年或者五年，到期来提，
He will withdraw it after three years or five.

只有一个条件，不管怎么样，要如数照付。』
There is only one condition: whatever happens, you must repay the full amount.”

『当然如数照付；
“Of course we repay the full amount.

还能怎么样？』
What else could we do?”

『老张，你没有听懂我的意思，也还不明白其中的利害。
“Old Zhang, you have not understood what I mean, nor what is at stake.

抄家你总晓得的，
You know what happens when a household’s property is confiscated.

被抄的人，倘或有私财寄顿在别处，照例是要追的。
Any private assets entrusted elsewhere are ordinarily pursued as well.

现在就是说，这笔存款，即使将来让官府追了去；你也要照付。
What I mean is that, even if the authorities recover this deposit from you, you must still repay the depositor.

请问你敢不敢担这个风险？』
Would you dare accept that risk?”

这一说，张胖子方始恍然，
Only now did Zhang see.

『我不敢！』他大摇其头，
“I would not!” he said, shaking his head vigorously.

『如果有这样的情形，官府来追，不敢不报，
“If the authorities came looking for the money, we would have to disclose it.

不然就是隐匿逆产，不得了的罪名。
Otherwise we should be guilty of concealing rebel property—a terrible charge.

等一追了去，人家到年限来提款，你怎么应付？』
Once they had taken it away, how could we pay the man when his deposit matured?”


『我晓得你不敢！』胡雪岩说∶『我敢！
“I knew you would not dare,” Hu said. “I would.

为啥呢？
Why?

我料定将来不会追。』
Because I am certain they will not pursue it.”

『喔，
“Oh?

何以见得？
What makes you so sure?

你倒说个道理我听所。』
Let me hear your reasoning.”

『何用说道理？
“What reasoning is needed?

打长毛打了好几年了，活捉的长毛头子也不少；
We have been fighting the Longhairs for years and have taken plenty of their leaders alive.

几时看官府追过。』
When have you seen the authorities trace their assets?”

胡雪岩放低了声音又说∶『你再看看，官军捉着长毛，自然搜括一空，根本就不报的，
He lowered his voice. “Look at the imperial troops. Once they catch a Longhair, they strip him of everything and never report it.

如果要追，先从搜括的官军追起；
If anyone traced the property, they would have to begin with the troops who plundered it.

那不是自己找自己麻烦？
Would that not be making trouble for themselves?

我说过，长毛的气数快尽了！
As I said, the Longhairs’ days are nearly over.

好些人都在暗底下盘算；
Many are laying secret plans.

他们还有一场劫，只要逃过这场劫，后半辈子就可以衣食无忧了。』
There is still one catastrophe for them to survive; once through it, they can live in comfort for the rest of their days.”

『是怎么样一场劫？』
“What catastrophe?”

『这场劫就是太平天国垮台。
“The fall of the Taiping Heavenly Kingdom.

一垮台，长毛自然变成「过街老鼠」，人人喊打，
Once it collapses, the Longhairs will be like rats crossing the street, with everyone shouting to strike them down.

在那一阵乱的时候最危险；
That first confusion will be the most dangerous time.

只要局面一定，朝廷自然降旨；首恶必惩，胁从不问，
Once order is restored, the court will naturally issue an edict: punish the ringleaders, spare those forced to follow.

更不用说追他们的私产。
Still less will it pursue their private property.

所以说，只要逃过这场劫，后半辈子就可以衣食无忧。』
That is why I say that, if they survive that catastrophe, they can live free of want for the rest of their lives.”

谈到这里，张胖子恍然大悟。
Now Zhang understood everything.

搜括饱了的长毛，要逃这场劫有个逃法，一是保命，二是保产。
The Longhairs who had gorged themselves on plunder needed two kinds of protection against the coming disaster: protection for their lives and for their wealth.

大劫来时即令逃得了命，也逃不了财产。
When it came, they might escape alive but lose their property.

换句话说，保命容易保产难；
In other words, saving their lives was easier than saving their wealth.

所以要早作安排。
Hence the need to arrange matters early.


想通了，不由得连连称『妙！』
Once he saw the scheme, Zhang could not help exclaiming, “Excellent! Excellent!”

但张胖子不是点头，而是摇头，
Yet he shook his head instead of nodding.

『老胡，』他带着些杞人忧天的味道∶『你这种脑筋动出来，要遭天忌的！』
“Old Hu,” he said, with something of the man who feared the sky might fall, “such ingenuity may provoke Heaven’s jealousy!”

『这也不足为奇！
“There is nothing so extraordinary about it.

我并没有害人的心思为啥遭天之忌？』
I mean no one harm. Why should Heaven be jealous?”

『那末，犯不犯法呢？』
“But is it against the law?”

张胖子自觉这话说得太率直；赶紧又解释∶『老胡，我实在因为这个法子太好了。
Feeling he had spoken too bluntly, Zhang hurried to explain. “Old Hu, it is because the scheme is so good.

俗语说的是∶好事多磨！
As the saying goes, good things meet many obstacles.

深怕其中有办不通的地方；
I am afraid there may be something that makes it unworkable.

有点不大放心。』
I cannot feel quite at ease.”

『你这话问得不错的。
“You are right to ask.

犯法的事，我们不能做；
We cannot break the law.

不过，朝廷的王法是有板有眼的东西，他怎么说，我们怎么做，这就是守法。
But the court’s laws are definite things: we do what they say, and that is obeying the law.

他没有说，我们就可以照我们自己的意思做。
Where they say nothing, we may follow our own wishes.

隐匿罪犯的财产，固然犯法；
Concealing a criminal’s property is certainly illegal.

但要论法，我们也有一句话说∶人家来存款的时候，额头上没有写着字∶我是长毛。
But if it is a question of law, we have an answer: when a man comes to make a deposit, he does not have ‘I am a Longhair’ written on his forehead.

化名来存，哪个晓得他的身分？
If he deposits under an assumed name, who knows his identity?”

『『其实我们晓得的，
“In fact, we do know.

良心上总说不过去！』
Our consciences cannot accept that.”


『老张，老张！』
“Old Zhang, Old Zhang!”

胡雪岩喝口酒，又感叹，又欢喜地说∶『我没有看错人，
Hu took a sip, at once moved and pleased. “I was not mistaken in you.

你本性厚道，
You are good-hearted by nature.

实在不错。
That is excellent.

然而要讲到良心；生意人的良心，就只有对主顾来讲。
But as for conscience, a merchant’s conscience concerns his customers.

公平交易，老少无欺，就是我们的良心。
Fair dealings, cheating neither young nor old—that is our conscience.

至于对朝廷，要做官的讲良心。
Officials must have a conscience towards the court.

这实在也跟做生意跟主顾讲良心是一样的道理，
It is really the same principle as a merchant’s duty to his customers.

「学成文武艺，卖与帝王家」，
‘Master the arts of letters and arms, then sell them to the imperial house.’

朝廷是文武官儿的主顾，是他们的衣食父母，
The court is the customer of civil and military officials; it feeds and clothes them.

不能不讲良心。
They cannot disregard their consciences towards it.

在我们就可以不讲了。』
We need not consider conscience in that way.”

『不讲良心讲啥？』
“What should we consider, then?”

『讲法，
“The law.

对朝廷守法，就是对朝廷讲良心。』
To obey the court’s laws is to satisfy our conscience towards the court.”

张胖子点点头，喝着酒沉思；
Zhang nodded and drank in thought.

好一会才欣然开口∶『老胡，我算是想通了。
After a long while, he spoke with pleasure. “Old Hu, I think I understand at last.

多少年来我就弄不懂，士农工商，为啥没好奸士、奸农、奸工、只有奸商？
For years I have wondered: among the four callings—scholar, farmer, craftsman and merchant—why does one hear of dishonest merchants, but not dishonest scholars, farmers or craftsmen?

可见得做生意的人的良心，别有讲究；
Evidently, a merchant’s conscience needs a different explanation.

不过要怎么个讲究，我想不明白。
I could never work out what it was.

现在明白了！
Now I understand.

对朝廷守法、对主顾讲公平，就是讲良心；就不是奸商！』
Obey the court’s laws and treat customers fairly: that is conscience, and that keeps one from being a dishonest merchant.”

『一点不错！
“Exactly!

老实说一句∶做生意的守朝廷的法，做官的对朝廷有良心，一定天下太平。
To speak plainly, if merchants obeyed the court’s laws and officials were conscientious towards it, the world would certainly be at peace.

再说一句∶只要做官的对朝廷讲良心，做生意的就不敢不守法。
More than that: if officials were conscientious, merchants would not dare disobey the law.

如果做官的对朝廷没有良心，要我们来对朝廷讲良心，未免迂腐。』
When officials have no conscience towards the court, to demand that merchants supply it is mere pedantry.”

『嗯，嗯；
“Yes, yes.

你这句话，再让我来想一想。』
Let me think that through.”

张胖子一面想，一面说∶『譬如，有长毛头子抓住了，抄家；
Zhang spoke as he reflected. “Suppose a Longhair leader is captured and his household’s property confiscated.

做官的抹煞良心，侵吞这个人的财产，
An official stifles his conscience and pockets the property.

那就是不讲良心。
That is acting without conscience.

如果我们讲良心呢？
But if we act conscientiously?

长毛化名来存款，说是应该充分的款子，我们不能收。
A Longhair offers a deposit under an assumed name, and we refuse because the money ought to be confiscated.

结果呢？
What is the result?

白白便宜赃官；仍旧让他侵吞了。
We simply benefit a corrupt official, who pockets it all the same.

对！』
Exactly!”

他一拍桌子，大声说道∶『光是做生意的对朝廷讲良心，没有用处。
He slapped the table and raised his voice. “It is no use for merchants alone to be conscientious towards the court.

我们只要守法就够了！』
Obeying the law is enough!”

『老张啊！』
“Old Zhang!”

胡雪岩也欣然引杯，
Hu too raised his cup with pleasure.

『这样才算是真正想通。』
“Now you have truly understood.”


这一顿酒吃得非常痛快；最后是张胖子抢着做的东。
They thoroughly enjoyed their drinking, and in the end Zhang insisted on paying.

分手之时，胡雪岩特别关照，他要趁眷属未到上海来的这两天，将钱庄和阿祥的事安排好；
Before they parted, Hu gave him a particular reminder: he wanted the bank and A’xiang’s affairs settled during the next few days, before his family reached Shanghai.

因为全家劫后重聚，他打算好好陪一陪老母，
Once they were reunited after their ordeals, he meant to spend proper time with his aged mother.

那时什么紧要的大事都得搁下来。
Even the most pressing business would have to be put aside.

张胖子诺诺连声；
Zhang agreed repeatedly.

一回到家先跟妻子商议，那爿小杂货店如何收束？
On arriving home, he first consulted his wife about winding up their little grocery.

他妻了倒也是有些见识的，
She had some judgement of her own.

听了丈夫的话，又高兴，又伤感；
His account made her both happy and wistful.

走进卧房，开箱子取出一个棉纸包，
Going into the bedroom, she opened a chest and took out a packet of soft cotton paper.

打开来给张胖子看，是一支不甚值钱的银镶风藤镯子。
She unwrapped it to show him a cheap vine bracelet mounted in silver.

做丈夫的莫名其妙，
Her husband was puzzled.

这支镯子与所谈的事有何相干？
What could it have to do with their discussion?

而张太太却是要从这上头谈一件往事，
But Mrs Zhang wished to tell an old story.

『这支镯子是雪岩的！
“This bracelet is Xueyan’s.

就在这支镯子上，我看出他要发达。』
It was this that showed me he would prosper.

她说，『这还是他没有遇到王抚台的时候的话；
It happened before he met Governor Wang.

那时他钱庄里的饭碗敲破了。日子很难过。
He had lost his job at the bank and was having a very hard time.

有一天来跟我说，他有个好朋友从金华到杭州来谋事，病在客栈里；
One day he told me that a good friend had come from Jinhua to seek work in Hangzhou and fallen ill at an inn.

房饭钱已经欠了半个月，还要请医生看病；
He owed a fortnight’s room and board and still needed a doctor.

没有五两银子不能过门，
Without five taels he could not get through.

问我能不能帮他一个忙？
Could I help?

我看雪岩虽然落魄，那副神气不象倒霉的样子；
Though Xueyan was down in the world, he did not have the air of a beaten man.

一件竹布长衫，虽然褪了色，也打过补钉，照样浆洗得蛮挺括，
His cotton gown was faded and patched, but washed and starched as neatly as ever.

见得他家小也是贤慧能帮男人的。
That showed he had a capable, virtuous wife to support him.

就为了这一点，我「嗯顿」都不打一个，借了五两银子给他。』
For that reason, I lent him five taels without a moment’s hesitation.”

『咦！』
“Really!”

张胖子大感兴趣，
Zhang was fascinated.

『还有这么一段故事，倒没听你说过。
“There was such a story, and you never told me!

钱，后来还你没有？』
Did he repay you?”


『你不要打岔，
“Do not interrupt.

听我说！』张太太说∶『当时雪岩对我说∶』现在我境况不好。
Listen!” Mrs Zhang continued. “Xueyan told me, ‘I am in poor circumstances now.

这五两银子不知道啥时候能还；不过我一定会还。
I do not know when I can repay these five taels, but I certainly shall.’

「说老实话，我肯借给他，自然也不打算他一时会还，
To be honest, since I was willing to lend, I naturally did not expect repayment at once.

所以我说∶『不要紧！
So I said, ‘Never mind.

等你有了还我。」
Repay me when you have it.’

他就从膀子上勒下这只风藤镯子，交到我手里∶』镯子连一两银子都不值。
Then he pulled this vine bracelet off his arm and put it in my hand. ‘It is not worth even one tael,’ he said.

不能算押头；
‘It cannot count as security.

不过这只镯子是我娘的东西，我看得很贵重。
But it belonged to my mother, and I value it greatly.

这样子做，是提醒我自己，不要忘记掉还人家的钱。
This will remind me not to forget to repay what I owe.’

「我不肯要，他一定不肯收回，就摆了下来。
I refused it, but he absolutely would not take it back, so he left it here.”

『』这不象雪岩的为人，
“That does not sound like Xueyan.

他说了话一定算数的。
He always keeps his word.”

『』你以为镯子摆在我这里，就是他没有还我那五两银子？
“You think that because the bracelet is still here, he never repaid the five taels?

不是的！
Not at all!

老早就还了。
He paid them back long ago.”

『』什么时候？
“When?”

『『就在他脱运交运，王抚台放到浙江来做官，没有多少时候的事。』
“Soon after his luck turned, when Governor Wang was appointed to Zhejiang.”

『那末镯子怎么还在你手里呢？』
“Then why do you still have the bracelet?”


『这就是雪岩做人，不能不服他的道理。
“That is what you cannot help admiring about him.

当时他送来一个红封套，里头五两银子银票；另外送了四色水礼。
He brought a red envelope containing a banknote for five taels, with four kinds of modest gifts besides.

我拿镯子还他，他不肯收；
When I offered the bracelet, he refused it.

他说∶现在的五两银子决不是当时的五两银了；
Five taels now, he said, were nothing like five taels then.

他欠我的情，还没有报。
The kindness he owed me had not been repaid.

这只镯子留在我这里，要我有啥为难的时候去找他，
He wanted me to keep the bracelet and come to him if I ever had a difficulty.

等帮过我一个忙，镯子才肯收回。
Only after he had helped me would he accept it back.

我想，他娘现在带金带翠，也不在乎一个风藤镯子；
I thought his mother must be wearing gold and jade by then and would hardly miss a vine bracelet.

无所谓的事了，所以我就留了下来。
It seemed of little consequence, so I kept it.

那次他帮你一个大忙，我带了四样礼去看他，特为去送镯子。
When he did you that great favour, I took four gifts to visit him, specially to return it.

他又不肯收。』
Again he refused.”

『这是啥道理？』
“What was his reason?”

张胖子越感兴味，
Zhang was more interested than ever.

『我倒要听听他又是怎么一套说法？』
“I should like to hear what he had to say this time.”

『他说，他帮你的忙，是为了同行的义气；
“He said he had helped you out of loyalty to a fellow banker.

再说男人在外头的生意，不关太太的事。
Besides, a man’s business outside the home did not concern his wife.

所以他欠我的情，不能「划帐」；
He could not cross off his debt to me against that account.

镯子叫我仍旧收着，
I was to keep the bracelet.

他将来总要替我做件称心满意的事，才算补报了我的情。』
One day he would do something to please me, and only then would my kindness be repaid.”

『话倒也有道理。
“There is sense in that.

雪岩这个人够味道就在这种地方，
This is what makes Xueyan such a fine fellow.

明明帮你的忙，还要教你心里舒坦。
He plainly does you a favour and makes you feel comfortable about it too.

闲话少说，
But enough talk.

我们倒商量商量看，这爿杂贷店怎么样交出去了』张胖子皱着眉说，
Let us consider how to hand over this grocery.” Zhang frowned.

『麻雀虽小，五脏俱全；
“Small as a sparrow, but with all its organs intact!

人欠欠人的帐目，鸡零狗碎的，清理起来，着实好有几天头痛。』
All the little sums owing to us and owing from us—it will give me days of headaches to sort them out.”

『头痛，
“Headaches?

为啥要头痛？
Why should it?

人欠欠人都有帐目的，
Everything is in the books.

连店址带货色「一脚踢」；
Transfer the premises, the stock and the accounts in one lot.

我们「推位让国」都交给了人家，拍拍身子走路，
We shall abdicate and surrender our little kingdom, hand everything over and brush ourselves off as we walk away.

还不轻松？』
What could be easier?”

张胖子大喜，
Zhang was delighted.

『对！
“Exactly!

还是你有决断。』
You are the decisive one.

他说，『明天雪岩问我盘这爿店要多少钱？我就说，我是一千六百块洋钱下本，仍旧算一千六百块好了。』
When Xueyan asks tomorrow how much I want for the shop, I shall say that I started it with sixteen hundred silver dollars and will take sixteen hundred for it.”

这套说法完全符合张太太的想法。
This accorded perfectly with his wife’s wishes.

三四年的经营，就这片刻间决定割舍；夫妇俩都无留恋之意，
In those few moments, they decided to part with the business they had built for three or four years, and neither felt any reluctance.

因为对『老本行』毕竟有根深蒂固的感情在，而且又是跟胡雪岩在一起。
Their attachment to the old trade was deeply rooted, after all, and he would be working with Hu Xueyan.

相形之下，这爿小杂货店就不是『鸡肋』而是『敝屣』了。
Beside that prospect, the little grocery was no chicken rib, too poor to relish but too good to throw away. It was a worn-out shoe, to be discarded without a thought.



胡雪岩 · 红顶商人
The Red-Topped Merchant
第七章（本章第1部分，共4部分）
逐句中英对照
原著：高阳


第七章
CHAPTER SEVEN


一早起身，张胖子还保持着多年的习惯，提着鸟笼上茶店；
On rising early, Fatty Zhang followed the habit of many years and took his birdcage to the teahouse.

有时候经过魏老板那里，因为同行的缘故，也打个招呼。
Sometimes, passing Mr Wei’s shop, he would stop to greet a fellow tradesman.

魏老板克勤克俭，从来不上茶店；但张胖子这天非邀他去吃茶不可，因为做媒的事，当着阿巧不便谈。
Wei was industrious and frugal and never went to teahouses, but that morning Zhang was determined to take him out for tea: the proposed marriage could hardly be discussed in A’qiao’s presence.

踏进店堂，开门见山道明来意，
Entering the shop, he stated his immediate purpose plainly.

魏老板颇有突然之感；因而便有辞谢之意。
Wei was taken by surprise and inclined to decline.

就在这时候，阿巧替她父亲来送早点，一碗豆腐浆，一团粢米饭，
Just then A’qiao brought her father breakfast, a bowl of soy milk and a ball of glutinous rice.

看到张老板甜甜地招呼∶『张伯伯早！
Seeing their visitor, she greeted him sweetly. “Good morning, Uncle Zhang!

点心吃过没有？』
Have you had breakfast?”


张胖子不即回答，
Zhang did not answer at once.

将她从头看到脚，真有点相亲的味道；看得阿巧有些发窘。
He looked her over from head to foot, very much as though appraising a prospective bride, until she grew embarrassed.

但客人还未答话，不便掉身而去；
Since he had not yet answered her greeting, however, she could hardly turn and leave.

只有将头扭了开去，避开张胖子那双盯住了看的眼睛。
She merely averted her face from his fixed gaze.

『阿巧！』张胖子问道，『你今年几岁？』
“A’qiao,” he asked, “how old are you this year?”

『十七。』
“Seventeen.”

『生日当然是七月初七。
“Your birthday is naturally the seventh day of the seventh month.

时辰呢？』
At what hour were you born?”

这下惊了阿巧！
That startled her.

一早上门，来问时辰八字，不是替自己做媒是做啥？
What could a man mean by calling first thing in the morning and asking for her birth details except that he had come to arrange a match?

这样转着念头，立刻想到阿祥；也立刻就着慌了！
Her thoughts flew at once to A’xiang, and she panicked.

『那个要你来做啥断命的媒？』她在心中自语；
“Who asked you to come matchmaking and ruin my life?” she thought.

急急地奔到后面，寻着她母亲问道∶『张胖子一早跑来为啥？』
Hurrying to the back, she found her mother. “What has Fatty Zhang come for so early?”

『哪个张胖子？』
“Which Fatty Zhang?”


『还有哪个？
“Who else?

不就是同行冤家的张胖子！』
The one in the same trade as Father—his rival!”

『他来了？
“Has he come?

我不晓得啊！』
I did not know.”

『娘！』
“Mother!”

阿巧扯着她的衣服说∶『张胖子不晓得啥心思，
A’qiao clutched her clothes. “He is up to something.

又问生日，又问时辰。
First he asks my birthday, then my birth hour.

我——，』她顿一顿足说∶『我是不嫁的！
I—” She stamped her foot. “I am not getting married!

用不着啥人来罗嗦。』
No one need come meddling.”

这一说，做母亲的倒是精神一振；
Her mother, however, became interested at once.

不晓得张胖子替女儿做的媒，是个何等样人？
What sort of young man had Zhang found for her daughter?

当时便说∶『你先不要乱！
“Do not make a fuss yet.

等我来问问看。』
Let me ask.”


发觉母亲是颇感兴趣的神气，阿巧非常失望，也很着急。
Her mother’s interest disappointed and alarmed A’qiao.

她心里在想，此身已有所属，母亲是知道的，
Surely she knew that her daughter’s heart was already given.

平时对阿祥的言语态度，隐隐然视之为『半子』；
Her ordinary manner toward A’xiang had long hinted that she regarded him as half a son.

那就不但知道自己属意于什么人，而且这个人也是她所中意的。
She therefore knew whom A’qiao wanted and approved of him herself.

既然如此，何必又去『问问看』？
Why, then, should she still want to “ask”?

岂不是不明事理的老糊涂了？
Was she growing foolish and unreasonable in her old age?

苦的是心里这番话说不出口；也无法用任何暗示提醒她。
The trouble was that A’qiao could say none of this aloud, nor could she think of any hint that would remind her.

情急之下，只有撒娇；拉住她母亲的衣服不放。
In desperation she could only behave like a spoiled child, clinging to her mother’s clothes.

『不要去问！
“Do not ask!

狗嘴里吐不出象牙，
No ivory comes from a dog’s mouth.

没有啥好问的。』
There is nothing worth asking him.”

『问问也不要紧。
“What harm can it do?

你这样子做啥？』
Why are you behaving like this?”

母女俩拉拉扯扯，僵持着，也因循着；
Mother and daughter tugged at each other, delaying and reaching no conclusion.

而魏老板却因为情面难却，接受了张胖子的邀请，
Meanwhile, Wei had found it impossible to refuse Zhang’s invitation.

在外面提高了声音喊∶『阿巧娘！
From the front he raised his voice. “A’qiao’s mother!

你出来看店；
Come and mind the shop.

我跟张老板吃茶去了。』
I am going out for tea with Mr Zhang.”

这一下阿巧更为着急。
Now A’qiao was more anxious than ever.

原意是想母亲拿父亲叫进来，关照一句∶如果张胖子来做媒，不要理他。
She had meant her mother to call her father in and warn him not to listen if Zhang proposed a match.

不想要紧话未曾说清楚，白白耽误了功夫。
Instead, they had wasted precious time without making the important point clear.

如今一起去吃茶，当然是说媒；
Naturally, if the men went out for tea, they would discuss the marriage.

婚事虽说父母之命，而父亲可以做七分主，
Marriage was said to be decided by both parents, but seven-tenths of the authority lay with her father.

如果在茶店里糊里糊涂听信了张胖子的花言巧语，那就是一辈子不甘心的恨事。
If he carelessly swallowed Zhang’s honeyed words at the teahouse, she would have cause for resentment all her life.

念头风驰电掣般快，转到此处，
Her thoughts raced like lightning.

阿巧脱口喊道∶『爹，你请进来，
“Father, come inside!” she blurted out.

娘有要紧话说。』
“Mother has something important to say.”

魏老板听这一说，便回了进来；他妻子问他∶『张胖子是不是来替阿巧做媒？』
Wei returned, and his wife asked, “Has Fatty Zhang come to arrange a match for A’qiao?”


魏老板还未答话，阿巧接口∶『哪个要他来做啥媒？
Before he could answer, A’qiao broke in. “Who asked him to arrange any match?

我是不嫁的。』
I am not getting married.”

『咦！』
“Eh?”

魏老板看看妻子，又看看女儿，真有些莫名其妙了，
Wei looked from his wife to his daughter in genuine bewilderment.

『你们怎么想到这上头去了？』
“How did you come to think of that?”

阿巧耳朵灵，心思快，立刻喜孜孜地问道∶『那末，他来做啥呢？』
Quick-eared and quick-witted, A’qiao brightened at once. “Then what has he come for?”

『他说要跟我谈一笔生意。』
“He says he wants to discuss a piece of business.”

『谈生意？』他妻子问道∶『店里不好谈？』
“Business?” his wife asked. “Can he not discuss it in the shop?”

『我也是这么说。
“That is what I said.

他说他一早起来一定要吃茶，不然没有精神。
But he says he must have his morning tea or he has no energy.

我就陪他去吃一回也不要紧。』
There is no harm in my joining him for once.”

『好，好！』
“Very well!”

阿巧推一推她父亲，
A’qiao gave her father a little push.

『你老人家请！
“Off you go, then.

不过，只好谈主意，不好谈别的。』
But you may discuss business only—nothing else.”


这一去去了两个钟头还不回来；
Two hours passed, and he did not return.

阿巧心里有嘀咕，叫小徒弟到张胖子每天必到的那家茶店里去悄悄探望。
Uneasy, A’qiao sent the little apprentice to make a discreet inquiry at the teahouse Zhang visited every day.

须臾回转，张胖子跟魏老板都不在那里。
The boy soon came back: neither man was there.

这就显得可疑了。
This looked suspicious.

等到日中，依然不见魏老板的影子，
By noon there was still no sign of Wei.

母女俩等了好半天等不回来，只有先吃午饭。
Mother and daughter waited a long time, then decided to eat without him.

刚扶起筷子，魏老板回来了，满脸红光，也满脸的笑容。
They had just picked up their chopsticks when he appeared, his face flushed and wreathed in smiles.

阿巧又是欣慰又是怨∶『到哪里去了？』
A’qiao was relieved but reproachful. “Where have you been?

她埋怨着∶『吃饭也不回来！』
You did not even come home for lunch.”

『张胖子请我吃酒；
“Fatty Zhang invited me for a drink.

这顿酒吃得开心。』
A thoroughly enjoyable drink it was too.”

『啥开心？
“What was so enjoyable?

生意谈成功了？』
Did you settle the business?

阿巧问∶『是啥生意？』
What business was it?”

『不但谈生意，
“We discussed more than business.

还谈了别样。是件大事！』
There was something else—something important.”

魏老板坐下来笑道∶『你们猜得不错，
Wei sat down, smiling. “You guessed correctly.

张胖子是来替我们女儿做媒的。』
Zhang did come to arrange our daughter’s marriage.”

听到这里，阿巧手足发冷；
A’qiao’s hands and feet turned cold.

一下扑到母亲肩上，浑身抖个不住。
She threw herself against her mother’s shoulder and shook from head to foot.


魏老板夫妇俩无不既惊且毫！
Both parents were startled and alarmed.

问她是怎么回事？却又似不肯明说；
They asked what was wrong, but she seemed unwilling to explain.

只勉强坐了下来，怔怔地望着她父亲。
With an effort she sat down again and stared at her father.

到底知女莫若母，毕竟猜中了她的心事；
No one knew a daughter better than her mother, who at last guessed what was troubling her.

急急向丈夫说∶『张胖子做媒，你不要乱答应人家。』
“You must not agree carelessly to a match Fatty Zhang proposes,” she told her husband urgently.

『为啥不答应？』
“Why should I not agree?”

『你答应人家了！
“You have agreed already?

是怎么样的人家；
What sort of family is it?

新郎倌什么样子？』
What is the bridegroom like?”

『新郎倌什么样子，何用我说？
“Why should I tell you what he is like?

你们天天看见的。』
You see him every day.”


提到每天看到的人，第一个想起的是间壁水果店的小伙计润生，
The first person A’qiao thought of was Runsheng, the young assistant at the fruit shop next door.

做事巴结，生得也还体面；
He worked hard and was quite presentable.

他有一手『绝技』，客人上门买只生梨要扦皮，润生手舞两把平头薄背的水果刀，旋转如飞，
He also had a remarkable skill: if a customer bought a pear and wanted it peeled, Runsheng would set two thin-backed, flat-tipped fruit knives whirling in his hands.

眼睛一霎的功夫，扦得干干净净，梨皮成一长条。
In the blink of an eye the pear was bare, its skin removed in one long strip.

陈巧最爱看他这手功夫；他也最爱看阿巧含笑凝视的神情。
A’qiao loved to watch him do it, and he loved to see her gazing at him with a smile.

有一次看得出神失了手，自己削掉一小节指头；
Once he had become so absorbed in looking at her that his hand slipped and he sliced off a small piece of his finger.

一条街上传为笑谈。
The whole street had made a joke of it.

以此话柄为嫌，阿巧从此总是避着他；
To avoid further gossip, she had kept out of his way ever since.

但彼此紧邻，无法不天天见面，润生颇得东家的器重，
But the shops were neighbors, so they could not help seeing each other daily, and his employer thought highly of him.

当然是可能来求婚的。
It was quite possible that he had asked for her.

第二个想起的是对面香蜡店的小开，
The second person she thought of was the son of the incense-and-candle shop owner opposite.

生得倒是一表人才，而且门当户对，可惜终年揭不得帽子；因为是个癞痢。
He was handsome, and their families were well matched, but he could never remove his cap: his scalp was diseased and patchy.

阿巧想起来就腻味，赶紧抛开再想。
The thought repelled her, and she hurriedly cast him from her mind.


这一想就想到阿祥了；
Then she thought of A’xiang.

顿时面红心跳。
Her face flushed and her heart beat wildly.

要问问不出口，好在有她母亲，
She could not bring herself to ask, but fortunately her mother could.

『是哪个？』她问她丈夫。
“Who is it?” she asked her husband.

『还有哪个，
“Who else?

自然是阿祥！』
A’xiang, naturally.”

『祥』字刚刚出口，阿巧便霍地起身，躲了进去；脚步轻盈无比。
The name had scarcely left his lips when A’qiao sprang up and fled into the back, her feet light as air.

魏老板楞了一会，哈哈大笑。
Wei stared for a moment, then burst into laughter.

『笑啥？
“What are you laughing at?

快说！
Tell us!

阿祥怎么会托张胖子来做媒？
How did A’xiang come to ask Fatty Zhang to act as matchmaker?

他怎么说？你怎么答复他？
What did he say, and what did you answer?

从头讲给我们听。』
Begin at the beginning.”

这一讲，连『听壁脚』的阿巧在内，无不心满意足；喜极欲涕，
As the story unfolded, everyone—including A’qiao, listening from the other side of the wall—was entirely satisfied, so happy that tears seemed near.

心里都有句话∶『阿祥命中有贵人；遇见胡道台这样的东家！』
All shared the same thought: A’xiang had found a benefactor in an employer like Circuit Intendant Hu.

然而胡道台此时却还管不到阿祥的事；
Hu himself, however, could not attend to A’xiang’s affairs just then.

正为另一个阿巧在伤脑筋。
Another A’qiao was giving him a headache.


阿巧姐昨夜通宵不归；一直到这天早晨九点钟才回家。
Sister A’qiao had been out all night and had not returned until nine that morning.

问起她的行踪，她说心中气闷，昨天在一个小姊妹家谈了一夜。
Asked where she had been, she said she had felt depressed and spent the night talking at the home of an old friend.

她的『小姊妹』也都三十开外了，
These “young companions” of hers were all over thirty now.

不是从良；便是做了本家——老鸨。
They had either left the profession to marry or become proprietresses—in other words, madams.

如是从了良的『人家人』，不会容留她只身一个人过夜；一定在头天夜里就派人送了她回来。
If she had visited a woman who had married into a respectable household, the family would hardly have kept an unaccompanied visitor overnight; someone would have escorted her home the evening before.

这样看来，行踪就很有疑问了。
Her movements therefore looked suspicious.

于是胡雪岩不动声色地派阿祥去打听。
Without betraying his thoughts, Hu sent A’xiang to investigate.

阿巧姐昨天出门虽不坐家里轿子，但料想她也不会步行；
She had not used the household sedan chair, but he did not imagine she had walked.

所以阿祥承命去向弄堂口待雇的轿夫去探问。
A’xiang accordingly questioned the bearers waiting for hire at the mouth of the lane.

果然问到了；
He found what he wanted.

阿巧姐昨天是去了宝善街北的兆荣里，
She had gone to Zhaorong Lane, north of Baoshan Street.

那轿夫还记得她是在倒数第二家，一座石库门前下的轿。
The bearer remembered setting her down at a stone-framed doorway, the second house from the far end.

所谓『有里兆荣并兆富，近接公兴，都是平康路』，
As the saying went, “Zhaorong and Zhaofu, with Gongxing close beside—all are roads to the pleasure quarters.”

那一带的兆荣里、兆富里、公兴里是有名的纸醉金迷之地；
Those lanes were famous haunts of luxurious dissipation.

阿巧姐摒绝从人，私访平康，其意何居？
Why had A’qiao dismissed her attendants and visited them secretly?

着实可疑。
It was deeply suspicious.


要破这个疑团，除却七姑奶奶更无别人。
Only the Seventh Lady could solve the mystery.

胡雪岩算了一下，这天正是她代为布置新居，约定去看的第四天；
Hu counted the days: this was the fourth day since she had undertaken to furnish his new home, the day agreed upon for him to inspect it.

因而坐轿不到古家，直往画锦里而去。
He therefore took his chair directly to Huajin Lane instead of Gu’s house.

果然，屋子已粉刷得焕然一新；
Sure enough, the rooms had been repainted and looked entirely new.

七姑奶奶正亲自指挥下人，在安放簇新的红木家具。
The Seventh Lady herself was directing the servants as they arranged brand-new rosewood furniture.

三月底的天气，艳阳满院，相当燠热，
It was late in the third month; brilliant sunshine filled the courtyard, and the weather was quite warm.

七姑奶奶一张脸如中了酒似的，而且额上见汗，头发起毛，
Her face was flushed as if she had been drinking, her forehead beaded with sweat, and her hair coming loose.

足见劳累。
Plainly she had worked hard.

胡雪岩大不过意，兜头一揖，深深致谢；
Hu felt deeply indebted and made a profound bow of thanks.

七姑奶奶答得漂亮∶『小爷叔用不着谢我，
Her answer was graceful. “There is no need to thank me, Little Uncle.

老太太，婶娘要来了；
Your honored mother and my aunt—your wife—are coming.

我们做小辈的，该当尽点孝心。』
We of the younger generation ought to show our filial respect.”

说着，她便带领胡雪岩一间屋子、一间屋子去看；
She led him through the house, room by room.

不但上房布置得井井有条，连下房也不疏忽，应有尽有。
Not only were the family apartments arranged in perfect order; even the servants’ quarters had been supplied with everything necessary.

费心如此，作主人的除了没口夸赞以外，再不能置一词。
Such care left the owner nothing to do but praise it without reservation.

一个圈子兜下来，回到客厅喝茶休息，
After making the circuit, they returned to the drawing room to rest over tea.

这时候胡雪岩方始开口，细诉阿巧姐一夜的芳踪；向七姑奶奶讨主意。
Only then did Hu explain A’qiao’s movements the previous night and ask for advice.


事出突兀，她一时哪里有主意？
The matter was so unexpected that the Seventh Lady had no ready answer.

将胡雪岩所说的话，前前后后细想了一遍，觉得有几件事先要弄清楚。
She considered his account from beginning to end and decided that a few points must first be clarified.

『小爷叔，』她问∶『阿巧姐回来以后，对你是啥样子？
“Little Uncle, how did she behave toward you when she came back?

有没有发牢骚？』
Did she complain?”

『没有，
“No.

样子很冷淡。』
She was very cold.”

『有没有啥收拾细软衣服，仿佛要搬出去的样子？』
“Did she pack any clothes or valuables, as though she meant to move out?”

『也没有。』胡雪岩答说，
“No.

『坐在那里剥指甲想心事，好象根本没有看到我在那里似的。』
She just sat there picking at her nails and thinking, as if I were not in the room.”

就问这两句话便够了。
Those two questions were enough.

七姑奶奶慢慢点着头，自言自语似地说∶『这就对了！
The Seventh Lady nodded slowly, almost talking to herself. “That fits.

她一定是那么个主意！』
That must be her plan.”

由于刚才一问一答印证了回忆，胡雪岩亦已有所意会；然而他宁愿自己猜得不对，
The exchange had revived Hu’s own recollections, and he too had begun to understand, though he would rather have been wrong.

『七姐，』他很痛苦地问∶『莫非她跟她小姊妹商量好了，还要抛头露面，自己去「铺房间」？』
“Seventh Sister,” he asked painfully, “can she have arranged with her old companions to appear in public again—to open a courtesan establishment of her own?”

『贱货！』脱口骂了一句。
A curse escaped him. “The shameless woman!”


『小爷叔！这，我要替阿巧姐不服。』
“Little Uncle, there I must take her side.”

七姑奶奶的本性露出来了，义形于色地说∶『一个人总要寻个归宿。
The Seventh Lady’s nature asserted itself; righteous indignation showed in her face. “A person must find some settled place in life.

她宁愿做低服小，只为觉得自己出身不是良家，一向自由惯了的，受不得大宅门的拘束，
She is willing to accept a subordinate position, but she feels that, having come from outside respectable society and been accustomed to freedom, she could not bear the restrictions of a great household.

要在外头住；
She wants to live separately.

说起来也不算过分。
That is not an excessive request.

这一层既然办不到，只有另觅出路；
If it cannot be granted, she must find another way.

哪里来的还到哪里去，不也是顺理成间的事？
Is it not natural to return to the place she came from?

就算是从良，总亦不能喊个媒波来说∶』我要嫁人了，你替我寻个老公来！
Even if she wishes to marry, she can hardly summon a matchmaker and say, ‘I want a husband; find me one.’

「她」铺房间「自己不下水；
She could open an establishment without taking clients herself.

遇见个知心合意的，自订终身，
If she meets a suitable man who understands her, they can decide their own future.

倒是正办。
That would be a proper course.”

『听她一顿排揎，胡雪岩反倒心平气和了，
After this scolding, Hu grew calmer.

笑笑说道∶』其实她要这样子做，倒应该先跟七姐来商量。
He smiled. “If that is what she means to do, she ought to have consulted you first.”

『』跟我没商量！
“She has not consulted me.

我心里不反对她这样子做；口里没有赞成她再落火炕的道理。
In my heart I might not oppose it, but I could hardly say aloud that I approved of her returning to that pit of fire.

阿巧姐是聪明人，
She is a clever woman.

怎么会露口风？
Why should she give me a hint?

我现在倒担心一件事；怕她心里恨你，将来会有意塌你的台。
What worries me now is that she may resent you and deliberately damage your reputation afterward.”

『』怎么塌法？
“How?”

『胡雪岩苦笑着，』
Hu smiled bitterly.

只要她再落水，我的台就让她坍足了。『
“If she goes back into that life at all, my reputation will be damaged enough.”


『那还不算坍足。
“Not as badly as it could be.

明天她挂上一块「杭州胡寓」的牌子，
Suppose tomorrow she puts up a sign saying ‘The Hu Residence of Hangzhou.’

那才好看呢！』
Then you will have something to look at!”

一句话说得胡雪岩发楞。
Hu was stunned.

他也听人说过，这一两年夷场『花市』，繁盛异常，堂子里兴起一种专宰冤大头的花样，
He too had heard how, during the past year or two, the flourishing pleasure trade in the foreign settlement had developed a new device for fleecing wealthy fools.

找个初涉花丛，目炫于珠围翠绕；鼻醉于粉腻脂香；耳溺于嗷嘈弦管的土财主，
A provincial rich man, newly ventured among the flowers, would find his eyes dazzled by jewels and beauty, his nose intoxicated by powder and perfume, and his ears drowned in music.

筵前衾底，做足了宛转绸缪的柔态痴情；
At the banquet and beneath the quilts, the woman would lavish tender, clinging affection upon him.

到两情浓时，论及嫁娶，总说孤苦伶仃一个人，早已厌倦风生，只为『身背浪向』有几多债务，
When their feelings had ripened and marriage was mentioned, she would explain that she was lonely and without family, had long been weary of her life, and was held back only by debts incurred in the profession.

只要替她完了债，她就是他家的人，
If he paid those debts, she would belong to his household.

除此别无要求。
She asked for nothing else.


于是冤大头替她还债『卸牌子』，自此从良。
The gullible patron would pay, have her signboard taken down, and bring her out of the profession.

到一做了良家妇女，渐渐不安于室；百般需索，
Once installed as a respectable wife, however, she would gradually become restless at home, making endless demands.

贪壑难填，
Nothing could fill the gulf of her greed.

稍不如意，就会变脸，三天一小吵，五天一大吵，吵得这家人家的上上下下，六神不安。
Any slight disappointment brought a change of face; minor quarrels every three days and major ones every five left the entire household distraught.

冤大头这才知道上了恶当；
Only then would the victim realize how thoroughly he had been duped.

然而悔之晚矣！
But regret came too late.

少不得再花一笔钱，才能请她走路。
He would have to pay another sum to be rid of her.

这个花样名为『氵忽浴』。
The trick was known as “taking a cleansing bath.”

如果洗清了一身债务，下堂求去，两不相干，还算是有良心的；
If, having washed away her debts, she left his household and broke off all dealings, she still had some conscience.

有些积年妖狐，心狠手辣，
Other hardened foxes were more ruthless.

嫁而复出，还放不过冤大头，
Returning to the profession after marriage, they refused to release their victim.

顶着他的姓接纳生张熟魏；甚至当筵诉说她的嫁后光阴如何如何？或者这家人家的阴私家丑，
They received new and familiar patrons alike under his surname, even recounting over dinner what married life in his house had been like, or exposing its private secrets and scandals.

少不得又要花钱，才能无事。
More money would then be needed to purchase peace.


不过，阿巧姐总不致于如此绝情。
Surely A’qiao would not be so heartless.

胡雪岩问道∶『她这样子做，于她有什么好处？
“What good would it do her?” Hu asked.

她是理路极清楚的人；
“She is an exceptionally reasonable woman.

为啥要做这种损人不利己的事？』
Why would she harm another person without benefiting herself?”

『小爷叔这句话说得很实在；
“That is a very fair point.

阿巧姐应该不是这种人。
She ought not to be that sort of person.

事情到了这步田地，反倒好办了。
Now that matters have reached this stage, they are easier to settle.

小爷叔，你交给我，
Leave it to me, Little Uncle.

包你妥当。』
I guarantee that I shall arrange everything properly.

七姑奶奶接着又说∶『小爷叔，你这两天不要回去！
And do not go back for the next couple of days.

住在我这里，还是住在钱庄里；随你的便，
Stay at my house or at the bank, whichever you please.

就是不要跟阿巧姐见面。
Only do not see A’qiao.”

『胡雪岩实在猜不透她葫芦里卖的什么药？
Hu could not fathom her plan.

料知问亦无用；为今之计，只有丢开不管，听凭她去料理了。
He knew that questions would be useless; the only course was to put the matter aside and let her manage it.

于是他说∶『我住在钱庄里好了。
“I shall stay at the bank.

我请了张胖子做档手；
I have engaged Fatty Zhang as a senior clerk.

趁这两天功夫陪他在店里谈谈以后的生意。』
These two days will give me time to sit with him at the shop and discuss future business.”

『张胖子为人倒靠得住的。
“Zhang is a dependable man.

就这样好了！
Very well.

你去忙你的生意；
Attend to your business.

有事我会到阜康来接头。』
If anything arises, I shall find you at Fukang.”


当天下午，七姑奶奶就去看一个人；是尤五的旧相知怡情老二。
That afternoon the Seventh Lady went to see an old intimate of Brother You’s, the Second Miss of Yiqing House.

当年因为松江漕帮正在倒霉的时候，弟兄们生计艰难；身为一帮当家的尤五，岂可金屋藏娇？
Years earlier, when the Songjiang Grain-Boat Guild had fallen on hard times and its members could scarcely make a living, how could its leader establish a gilded nest for a favorite?

因而尽管怡情老二说之再三，尤五始终不肯为她『卸牌子』；
However often the Second Miss urged him, Brother You had refused to redeem her from the profession.

怡情老二一气之下，择人而事，嫁的是个破落的世家子弟，体弱多病，
Angry, she had chosen another man, a sickly son of an impoverished distinguished family.

不到两年呜呼哀哉。
He died within two years.

怡情老二没有替他守节的必要；事实上也不容于大妇，
She felt no obligation to remain a faithful widow; indeed, his principal wife would not tolerate her.

因而重张艳帜。先是做『先生』；后来做『本家』，
She therefore returned to the pleasure quarters, first as a courtesan and later as a proprietress.

跟尤五藕继丝连，至今不绝。
Her ties with Brother You had never quite been severed and continued to this day.


阿巧姐原是怡情老二房间里的人；
A’qiao had once worked in the Second Miss’s establishment.

七姑奶奶去看怡情老二，一则是要打听打听阿巧姐预备复出，到底是怎么回事？再则也是要利用她跟阿巧姐旧日的情分，从中斡旋。
The Seventh Lady sought her out partly to learn the truth about A’qiao’s supposed return to the trade and partly to enlist her old friendship as a means of mediation.

不过自己一个良家妇女，为了古应春的声名，不便踏入妓家；
But as a respectable married woman, she could not enter a courtesan house without compromising Gu’s reputation.

特意到相熟的一家番菜馆落脚，托西崽去请怡情老二来相会。
She went instead to a familiar Western restaurant and asked a waiter to invite the Second Miss to meet her there.

两个人有大半年不曾见面了。
They had not seen each other for more than half a year.

由于彼此的感情，一向很好，所以执手殷勤，叙不尽的寒温。
Their affection had always been strong, and they clasped hands warmly, with endless inquiries and greetings.

怡情老二问讯了七姑奶奶全家，与尤五以外，也问起胡雪岩；这恰好给了她一个诉说的机会。
After asking about the Seventh Lady’s family and Brother You, the Second Miss also asked after Hu, giving her visitor just the opening she needed.

『我今天就是为我们这位小爷叔的事，要跟你商量。』
“It is on Little Uncle’s account that I want to consult you today.

七姑奶奶说∶『阿巧姐跟胡老爷要分手了。』
A’qiao and Mr Hu are going to part.”

『为啥？』怡情老二讶然相问∶『为啥合不来？』
“Why?” the Second Miss asked in surprise. “Why can they not get along?”

『其实也没有啥合不来——。』七姑奶奶将家眷属脱困，将到上海；谈到阿巧姐的本心。
“There is really no quarrel between them—” The Seventh Lady explained that Hu’s family had escaped and was coming to Shanghai, then described A’qiao’s wishes.

语气中一直强调，脱辐已成定局，姻缘无可挽救。
Throughout, she emphasized that the separation was settled and the relationship could not be saved.

怡情老二凝神听完，面现困惑，
The Second Miss listened attentively, looking puzzled.

『阿巧姐跟我，一两个月总要见一次面；
“A’qiao and I meet every month or two.

这样的大事，她怎么不来跟我谈？』
Why has she not discussed something so important with me?

她问∶『她跟胡老爷分手以后怎么办？
What will she do after leaving Mr Hu?

苏州又回不去；而且乡下她也住不惯的。』
She cannot return to Suzhou, and she is not used to country life.”

『是啊！』七姑奶奶接口说道∶『不管她怎么样，我们大家的情分总在的；
“Exactly,” the Seventh Lady agreed. “Whatever she does, our friendship remains.

就是胡老爷也很关心她。
Even Mr Hu is concerned for her.

一个女流之辈，孤零零地，总要有个妥当的安顿之处才好。
A woman alone must have somewhere suitable to settle.

她自己好象打定了主意；不过，这个主意照我看不大高明。
She seems to have made up her mind, but I do not think her plan is wise.

二阿姐，你晓不晓得她在兆富里有没有要好的小姊妹？』
Second Sister, do you know whether she has any close friends in Zhaofu Lane?”



胡雪岩 · 红顶商人
The Red-Topped Merchant
第七章（本章第2部分，共4部分）
逐句中英对照
原著：高阳


怡情老二想了一下答说∶『有的。
The Second Miss thought for a moment. “Yes.

她从前没有到我这里来之前，在心想红老六那里帮忙；
Before she came to my establishment, she worked for the Sixth Miss of Xinxianghong House.

跟同房间的阿金很谈得来。
She was very friendly with A’jin, who worked there too.

阿金我也认识的，
I know A’jin as well.

现在就住在兆富里，养着个小白脸。』
She lives in Zhaofu Lane now and keeps a handsome young lover.”

『这个阿金，现在做啥？』
“What does she do nowadays?”

『现在也是铺房间。』
“She runs an establishment herself.”

『我猜得恐怕不错。』
“Then I may have guessed correctly.”

七姑奶奶将阿巧姐瞒着人私访兆富里的经过，细细说了一遍，推断她是跟阿金在商量，也要走这条路。
The Seventh Lady described A’qiao’s secret visit to Zhaofu Lane and explained her inference that she had gone to discuss following the same path.

『奇怪！
“How strange!

她为什么不来跟我商量？』
Why did she not consult me?”

『二阿姐，你问得对。
“That is a fair question, Second Sister.

不过，我倒要请问你，如果阿巧姐要走这条路，你赞成不赞成？』
But let me ask you: if A’qiao wanted to do such a thing, would you approve?”

『我怎么会赞成？
“How could I?

这碗饭能不吃最好不吃！』
Anyone who can avoid earning a living that way should do so.”

『那就对了。
“There you have it.

她晓得你不会热心，
She knew you would not be enthusiastic.

何必来跟你商量？』
Why should she consult you?”

『这话倒也是。』
“That is true.”

怡情老二仍然困惑∶『我就不懂。她为啥还要回头来「触祭」这碗断命饭？』
The Second Miss was still puzzled. “I simply cannot understand why she should return to that wretched livelihood.”


七姑奶奶认为要商量的正就是这一点。
That, the Seventh Lady felt, was precisely what they must discuss.

猜测阿巧姐预备重堕风尘的动机，不外三种∶第一是为生计所逼；第二是报复胡雪岩；第三是借此为阅人之地，要好好觅个可靠的人，为一世的归宿。
If A’qiao intended to return to the pleasure quarters, there could be only three motives: the need to support herself, revenge upon Hu, or a wish to use the place to meet men and find a dependable partner for life.

『我在想，』七姑奶奶分析过后，谈她自己的意见∶『第一，她不必愁日子不好过，
Having analyzed the possibilities, she gave her own view. “First, she need not worry about money.

她自己跟我说过，手里有两三万银子的私房；
She told me herself that she has twenty or thirty thousand taels put away.

而况分手的时节，胡老爷总还要送她一笔钱。
Besides, Mr Hu will certainly give her another sum when they part.

至于说到报复，到底没有深仇切恨，
As for revenge, there is no deep hatred between them.

要出人家的丑，自己先糟蹋名声出了丑；
To disgrace him, she would first have to disgrace herself.

她不是那种糊涂人。
She is not so foolish.

想来想去，只有这样子一个理由∶想挑个好客人嫁！』
The more I think of it, the more I can see only one explanation: she wants to choose a suitable patron to marry.”

『为了要嫁人，先去落水？
“Go back into that life in order to find a husband?

这种事从来没有听说过。』
I have never heard of such a thing.”

怡情老二大为摇头，
The Second Miss shook her head vigorously.

『除非象阿金那样，挑个小白脸养在小房子里；
“Unless she means to follow A’jin’s example and keep some handsome young man in a little house.

要挑好客人是挑不到的。』
She will never find a good patron to marry that way.”

这话可以分两方面来听，一方面听怡情老二始终是不信阿巧姐会出此下策的语气；另一方面亦可以听出她不以阿巧姐此举为然。
Her words could be understood in two senses: she still did not believe that A’qiao would adopt such a poor plan, and she certainly disapproved of it.

而无论从哪方面来听，都能使七姑奶奶感到欣慰的。
Either way, the Seventh Lady found them reassuring.


『二阿姐，我亦不相信七阿巧姐会走上这条路。
“I too can hardly believe that A’qiao would take that road.

不过，打开天窗说亮话，
But let us speak plainly, Second Sister.

我一面是帮我小爷叔的忙；一面也是为阿巧姐的好。
I am trying both to help Little Uncle and to do what is best for her.

二阿姐，这件事上头，你要看我五哥的分上，帮一帮我的忙！』
For Brother Five’s sake, you must help me with this.”

怡情老二有些不好意思地笑了，
The Second Miss smiled in embarrassment.

『七姑奶奶，说到这话，你该罚！
“You deserve a penalty for saying that!

你的吩咐，我还有个不听？』她质问着，
Would I ever refuse something you asked?

『为啥要搬到五少来？』
Why must you bring Fifth Master into it?”

『是我的话说得不对，
“I spoke wrongly.

你不要动气。
Do not be angry.

我们商量正经；
Let us discuss the real business.

我原有个主意——。』七姑奶奶是打算着一条移花接木之计，
I already had a plan—” The Seventh Lady intended to transplant the blossom onto another branch.

特地托号子里的秦先生，写信给宁波的张郎中，想撮合他与阿巧姐成就一头姻缘。
She had specially asked Mr Qin at the firm to write to Dr Zhang in Ningbo, hoping to arrange a marriage between him and A’qiao.

这话说来又很长；
There was a long story behind it.

怡情老二从头听起，得知张郎中如何与阿巧姐结识，以及后来落花有意，流水无情，怅然而返的经过，
The Second Miss listened from the beginning, learning how they had met and how the doctor, whose feelings had found no response, had returned home disappointed.

对此人倒深为同情。
She felt considerable sympathy for him.


『七姑奶奶，你这个主意，我赞成。
“I approve of your plan.

不过，是不是能够成功，倒难说得很。
But whether it can succeed is another matter.

男女之间，完全靠缘分；看样子，阿巧姐好象跟他无缘。』
Between a man and a woman, everything depends on affinity, and A’qiao does not seem to have any with him.”

『不是！
“That is not it.

当初是因为我小爷叔横在中间，
Little Uncle stood between them.

这面一片心都在他身上，张郎中再好也不会中意；
Her whole heart was fixed on him, so however good the doctor might be, she would never consider him.

那面，看阿巧姐是有主儿的，知难而退。
The doctor, for his part, saw that she already belonged to someone and withdrew before the obstacle.

其实，照我看，阿巧姐既然不愿意做人家的偏房，嫁张郎中就再好不过。
As I see it, if she is unwilling to become a concubine, she could do no better than marry him.

第一，张郎中的太太最近去世了，
First, his wife has recently died.

以他对阿巧姐那一片痴情来说，讨她回去做填房，也是肯的；
Given his devotion to A’qiao, he would be willing to take her as his new principal wife.

第二，张郎中年纪也不大。』
Second, he is not very old.

七姑奶奶问道∶『阿巧姐今年多少？』
How old is A’qiao now?”

『她属羊的。
“She was born in the year of the Sheep.

今年——，』怡情老二扳指头算了一下，失声惊呼∶『今年整四十了！』
This year—” The Second Miss counted on her fingers, then exclaimed in surprise. “Exactly forty!”

『她生得后生，四十倒看不出。
“She looks young; one would never guess forty.

不过总是四十了！』
But forty she is.”

七姑奶奶停了一下，歉然地说∶『二阿姐，我说一句你不要生气，四十岁的人，又是这样子的出身；只怕要做人家的正室，不大容易！』
The Seventh Lady paused, then added apologetically, “Do not be offended, Second Sister, but a woman of forty, with her background, cannot easily become a man’s principal wife.”

『岂止不大容易？
“Not easily?

打着灯笼去找都难。』
One could hardly find such a match with a lantern.

怡情老二很郑重地问道∶『七姑奶奶，张郎中那里，你有几分把握？』
Tell me seriously: how certain are you of the doctor?”

『总有个六七分。』
“Six or seven chances in ten, at least.”

『六七分是蛮有把握的了。
“That is fairly certain.

我今天就去看阿巧姐，问她到底是啥意思？
I shall see A’qiao today and ask what she means to do.

如果没有这样的打算，自然最好；
If she has no intention of returning to the trade, so much the better.

倘使有的，我一定要拦住她。
If she has, I must stop her.

总而言之，不管她怎么样打算，我一定要做个媒。』
Whatever she intends, I shall act as matchmaker.”

『你是女家的媒人，我是男家的。
“You will represent the bride, and I the groom.

我们一定拿它做成功也是件好事。』
We must make it succeed. It will be a good deed.”


『当然是好事。
“A good deed, certainly.

不过，好象委屈了张郎中。』
Though it seems rather unfair to the doctor.”

提到这一层。七姑奶奶想起自己嫁古应春以前，由胡雪岩居间安排，拜王有龄的老太太做义女的往事，
At that, the Seventh Lady remembered how, before she married Gu, Hu had arranged for Wang Youling’s mother to adopt her as a daughter.

顿时又有了灵感。
Inspiration came at once.

『二阿姐，既然你这样说，我们倒商量商量看，怎么样把阿巧姐的身分抬一抬？』
“Since you feel that way, Second Sister, let us consider how to raise A’qiao’s standing.”

七姑奶奶的安排是，请胡老太太收阿巧姐为义女；
Her plan was to ask Hu’s mother to adopt A’qiao.

于是胡雪岩便是以『舅爷』的身分唱一出『嫁妹』了。
Hu would then take the part of a brother marrying off his sister, receiving the honors due to the bride’s brother.

这原是古人常有之事，
Such arrangements had often been made in former times.

在此时此地来说，特别显得情理周至，
In their present circumstances, it seemed a particularly considerate and reasonable solution.

怡情老二自然赞成，也为阿巧姐高兴，认为这样子做，她倒是『修成正果』了。
The Second Miss naturally approved and rejoiced for A’qiao: through this, she thought, her long journey would reach a proper fulfillment.


七姑奶奶也很得意于自己的这个打算；
The Seventh Lady herself was delighted with the idea.

性子本来急，也正兴头的时候，当时就要邀怡情老二一起去看阿巧姐，当面锣、对面鼓，彻底说个明白。
Impatient by nature and now carried away by enthusiasm, she wanted to take the Second Miss straight to A’qiao and settle the whole matter face to face.

倒还是怡情老二比较持重，
The Second Miss was more cautious.

认为应该先跟阿金碰个头，打听清楚了邀她一起去谈，更容易使阿巧姐受劝。
She thought they should first see A’jin, establish the facts, and invite her to join them; A’qiao would then be more easily persuaded.

『那也好！』
“Very well.

七姑奶奶问道∶『我们就去看阿金。』
Let us go and see A’jin.”

『这——，』怡情老二知道阿金因为养着小白脸，忌讳生客上门；但这话不便明说，
“Well—” The Second Miss knew that A’jin disliked unfamiliar visitors because she kept a young lover, but she could hardly say so outright.

所以掉个枪花∶『七姑奶奶，你的身分不便到她那里。
She changed tack. “A woman of your standing should not go there.

我叫人去喊她来。』于是她唤带来的小大姐，赶到兆富里去请阿金；特别叮嘱喊一乘『野鸡马车』，坐催阿金一起坐了来。
I shall send for her.” She called the young maid who had accompanied her and sent her hurrying to Zhaofu Lane, with particular instructions to hire an ordinary street carriage and bring A’jin back in it without delay.

在这等候的当儿，少不得又聊家常。
While they waited, the two women naturally talked of their own affairs.

怡情老二的话中，颇有厌倦风尘之意；但也不曾表示要挑个什么样的人从良，
The Second Miss sounded weary of life in the pleasure quarters, yet said nothing of choosing a man to marry.

七姑奶奶思路快，口也快，听出她的言外之意，忍不住要提出诤劝。
Quick in both thought and speech, the Seventh Lady heard what lay beneath her words and could not resist offering candid advice.


『二阿姐，你不要一门心思不转弯，
“Second Sister, do not fix your mind on a single course and refuse to turn aside.

那样也太痴了！
That is too foolishly devoted.

你始终守着我五哥，守到头发白也不会成功。
If you go on waiting for Brother Five, you may wait until your hair is white and still achieve nothing.

这里头的原因，五哥想必跟你说过。
He must have told you why.

他领一帮，做事要叫人心服；
He leads a whole guild and must act in ways that earn its members’ respect.

弟兄穷得没饭吃，他还要多立一个门户，你想，这话怎么说得过去？
While they are too poor to feed themselves, how could he justify setting up another household?

二阿姐，你死了这条心吧！』
Give up that hope.”

怡情老二无词以对。
The Second Miss had no answer.

默然泫然，惟有背人拭泪。
Silent and tearful, she turned away to wipe her eyes.

七姑奶奶也觉得心里酸酸地好不自在；倒有些懊悔，不该拿话说得这么直。
The Seventh Lady too felt an ache of unhappiness and regretted having spoken so plainly.

『说真的，』她没话找话，用以掩饰彼此都感到的不自然，『那位张郎中倒是好人，家道也过得去；
“Truly,” she said, searching for something to ease their mutual embarrassment, “that doctor is a good man, and comfortably off.

我就怎么没有想到，
Why did I not think of it?

早应该替你做这个媒。』
I ought to have arranged a match for you long ago.”

『多谢你，七姑奶奶！
“Thank you.

命生得不好，吃了这碗断命饭；
But I was born to ill fortune and took up this wretched livelihood.

连想做小都不能够，
I cannot even become a concubine.

还说啥？』
What more is there to say?”

话中依然是怨怼之意。使得一向擅于词令的七姑奶奶也无法往下接口了。
Her words still held resentment, and the usually eloquent Seventh Lady could find nothing to add.


幸好，兆富里离此不远；
Fortunately, Zhaofu Lane was nearby.

一辆马车很快地去而复回，载来了阿金。
The carriage soon returned with A’jin.

她在路上便已听小大姐说过，所以一见七姑奶奶，不必怡情老二引见，很客气地问道∶『是尤家七姑奶奶？
The maid had explained matters on the way, so A’jin needed no introduction before greeting the Seventh Lady courteously. “You are the Seventh Lady of the You family?

生得好体面！』
What a fine-looking woman you are!”

『不敢当！
“You are too kind.”

这位，』七姑奶奶问怡情老二，
The Seventh Lady turned to her companion.

『想来就是阿金姐了？』
“Then this must be Sister A’jin?”

『是啊！』
“Yes.”

怡情老二做主人，先替阿金要了食物饮料；然后开门见山地说∶『七姑奶奶为了关心阿巧姐，特意请你来，想问问你；
Acting as hostess, the Second Miss ordered food and drink for the newcomer, then came straight to the point. “The Seventh Lady is concerned about A’qiao and has specially asked you here.

这两天阿巧姐是不是到你那里去了？』
Has A’qiao been to see you these past few days?”

『她常到我那里来的。』
“She comes to see me often.”

『阿金姐，』七姑奶奶说，『我们是初会，二阿姐知道我的，心直口快。
“Sister A’jin,” the Seventh Lady said, “we have not met before, but Second Sister knows me: I am frank and speak my mind.

我说话有不到的地方，请你不要见气。』
If I say anything clumsy, please do not take offense.”

这是因为阿金跟怡情老二，谈到阿巧姐时，一上来便有针锋相对之势；
A’jin and the Second Miss had seemed at odds as soon as A’qiao was mentioned.

七姑奶奶深怕言事碰僵，不但于事无补，反倒伤了和气，所以特为先打招呼。
The Seventh Lady feared that a collision would accomplish nothing and only damage their friendship, so she made this precautionary apology.

阿金也是久历风尘，熟透世故的人，
A’jin too had long experience of the world and understood its ways.

自知一句『她常到我这里来的』答语，语气生硬，隐含敌意，成为失言；
She knew that her stiff answer had carried a hint of hostility and had been ill judged.

所以歉然答道∶『七姑奶奶你言重了！
“Please do not say that.

我的嘴笨；
I am clumsy with words.

二阿姐又是好姊妹，说话不用客气。
Second Sister and I are old friends, so I do not stand on ceremony with her.

你可千万不能多我的心！』
You must not misunderstand me.”

既然彼此都谦抑为怀，就无须再多作解释，反倒象真的生了意见。
With both sides showing humility, further explanations would only suggest that there really was a quarrel.

不过，有些话，七姑奶奶因为彼此初交，到底不便深问；
Still, as a new acquaintance, the Seventh Lady could hardly press certain questions herself.

要由怡情老二来说，比较合适。
The Second Miss would be better placed to ask them.

因而报以一笑之外，向旁边抛了个眼色示意。
She smiled and gave her a meaningful glance.


怡情老二点点头，接下来便用平静的语气，向阿金说明原委∶『阿巧姐跟胡老爷生了意见。
The Second Miss nodded and explained calmly to A’jin. “A’qiao and Mr Hu have fallen out.

「清官难断家务事」，谁是谁非也不必去说它；
Even a wise magistrate cannot settle family troubles, so there is no need to decide who is right or wrong.

总而言之，恐怕是要分手了。
In short, they will probably separate.

七姑奶奶跟阿巧姐的感情一向是好的；当初作成他们的姻缘，又是七姑奶奶出过力的，
The Seventh Lady has always been close to A’qiao and helped bring them together in the first place.

不管怎么说，阿巧姐的事，她不能不关心。
Naturally, she cannot be indifferent to what happens now.

刚刚特地寻了我来问我；我实在不晓得。
She came specially to ask me, but I know nothing.

阿巧姐好久没有碰过头了，
I have not seen A’qiao for some time.

听说这两天到你那里去过，想必总跟你谈了，
Hearing that she had visited you in the last few days, I thought she must have told you something.

她到底有什么打算？』
What does she intend to do?”

『喔，』
“Oh.”

阿金听完，不即回答，
A’jin did not answer immediately.

却转脸问七姑奶奶，
Instead, she turned to the Seventh Lady.

『阿巧姐跟胡老爷的感情，到底怎么样？』
“How are things really between A’qiao and Mr Hu?”

『不坏啊！』
“Not bad.”


『那就奇怪了！』
“Then it is strange.”

阿金困惑地，
A’jin looked puzzled.

『她每次来，总怨自己命苦。
“Whenever she comes, she complains of her unhappy fate.

我问她∶胡老爷待你好不好？她总是摇头不肯说。
I ask whether Mr Hu treats her well, but she only shakes her head and refuses to say.

看样子——。』下面那句话，她虽不说，亦可以猜想得到。
From the look of things—” She left the next words unspoken, though their meaning was easy to guess.

这一下，却是轮到七姑奶奶有所困惑了；
Now the Seventh Lady was puzzled in turn.

『阿巧姐为啥有这样的表示？』她问，
“Why should she give that impression?

『他们要分手，也是最近的事；
This talk of parting is very recent.

只为胡老爷的家眷要到上海来了，大太太不容老爷在外面另立门户，
Mr Hu’s family is coming to Shanghai, and his principal wife will not allow him to keep a separate household.

阿巧且又不肯进她家的门，以致于弄成僵局。
A’qiao refuses to enter the family home, so they are at an impasse.

要说以前，看不出来他们有啥不和的地方！』
Before this, I could see no sign of disagreement between them.”

阿金点点头，
A’jin nodded.

『这也不去说它了。』
“Let us leave that aside.”

她的脸色阴沉了，
Her face grew gloomy.

『也许要怪我不好。
“Perhaps I am to blame.

我有个堂房姑婆，
I have a great-aunt on my father’s side, from a collateral branch of the family.

现在是法华镇白衣庵的当家师太；
She is now abbess of White-Robed Convent in Fahua Town.

一到上海，总要来看我，
Whenever she comes to Shanghai, she visits me.

有时候跟阿巧姐遇见，两个人谈得很起劲。
Sometimes she has met A’qiao here, and they have talked with great enthusiasm.

我们那位老师太，说来说去无非「前世不修今世苦」，劝她修修来世。
The old abbess is always saying that suffering in this life comes from a failure to cultivate virtue in the last, and urging her to prepare for a better life to come.

这也不过出家人的老生常谈；
It was only the usual talk of a religious person.

哪知道阿巧姐倒有些入迷的样子。』
